takeaways: A spring 2026 driving tour of Shakopee, one of the metro's oldest river towns and now one of its busiest for new building permits. Highway 169 runs through the middle, so you're never more than a few minutes from it.

Attractions: Valleyfair (celebrating its 50th year), Canterbury Park (horse racing and a 24/7 card casino), the new 19,000-seat Mystic Lake Amphitheater next door (the largest in Minnesota) and Murphy's Landing, a free living-history village on the Minnesota River with an 1844 Faribault house.

Around the amphitheater: about 1,000 new apartments, restaurants and Badger Hill Brewing. Historic downtown along Highway 101 has been revitalized, with older homes (late 1800s to about 1960, roughly 1,500 to 2,500 square feet) from the high $200,000s to mid-$400,000s.

Prices as stated in the video: mid-1990s townhomes about $225,000 to $280,000, existing single-family homes mostly in the mid-$300,000s to mid-$500,000s, and new construction townhomes from the low to mid-$300,000s and single-family homes from the low $500,000s to about $900,000. Homes on Lake O'Dowd, the city's only full recreational lake, run from about $800,000 to several million.
More than 70 miles of trails, 35 parks and a community center with an ice rink, indoor pool and fitness center. St. Francis Regional Medical Center is the largest hospital in the southwest metro.

About 20 to 25 minutes to MSP Airport, 25 to 30 minutes to downtown Minneapolis and about 35 to downtown Saint Paul. The Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community is restoring prairie land, complete with bison.

faq.q: How big is the new amphitheater in Shakopee?
faq.a: About 19,000 seats, the largest amphitheater in Minnesota, next to Canterbury Park, according to the video.

faq.q: Is there a lake in Shakopee?
faq.a: Lake O'Dowd is Shakopee's only full recreational lake, known for bass fishing, with homes from about $800,000 to several million dollars at the time of the video.

faq.q: How far is Shakopee from Minneapolis?
faq.a: About 25 to 30 minutes to downtown Minneapolis, about 35 minutes to downtown Saint Paul and 20 to 25 minutes to MSP Airport, depending on traffic.

takeaways: Six towns Jason thinks locals keep to themselves. Northfield: about 40 minutes south, home to St. Olaf and Carleton, the Cannon River and the Defeat of Jesse James Days each September.

Stillwater: an old logging town on the St. Croix River, with antique shops, the Lift Bridge, cave tours and riverboats, plus a mix of historic and new homes. Highway 36 upgrades make I-494/I-694 easy to reach.
New Prague: a historic town on the southwest edge with a newly rebuilt main street, surrounded by farmland, about 40 minutes from the airport.
North Oaks: a private community in the northeast metro where residents own the roads, with large wooded lots and mature oaks.
Mankato: a college town about 75 minutes south, with Minnesota State University, a historic downtown on the Minnesota River and a regional airport.
Excelsior: a walkable downtown on Lake Minnetonka with dining and lake excursions, and homes from about $400,000 into the millions.

faq.q: What are some charming small towns near the Twin Cities?
faq.a: Jason's picks are Northfield, Stillwater, New Prague, North Oaks, Mankato and Excelsior, each with a historic downtown or a distinct setting within about an hour or so of the metro.

faq.q: Who owns the roads in North Oaks?
faq.a: The residents do. North Oaks' roads are privately owned, one reason the community feels so secluded.

takeaways: A 2024 tour of a Cuddigan custom home in The Ranch, an acreage neighborhood in Credit River about 3 to 5 miles west of I-35 and about 20 minutes from the airport, with shopping close by.
About 5,000 square feet on roughly 2.5 acres: five bedrooms, five baths and a three-car garage. About 13 lots remained in Phase 1 at the time, with about 20 more planned for Phase 2.

The main level has whitewashed oak floors, a large island with a farm sink, Fisher & Paykel appliances, a full butler's pantry, a mudroom with lockers, an office, and a screened porch with a two-sided fireplace between decks.

Upstairs are a loft, laundry and four bedrooms, including two with private baths and an owner's suite with a large custom closet. The lower level adds a wet bar, a golf simulator, an exercise room, a fifth bedroom and a patio, with two heating zones.

faq.q: How big are the lots in The Ranch in Credit River?
faq.a: About 2.5 acres or more, according to the video.

takeaways: A 2025 listing tour, with Jason and Brooke Huerkamp, of an 1885 brownstone in Saint Paul's Cathedral Hill area: just over 3,000 square feet, three bedrooms, three baths and a two-car garage.
The home was taken down to the studs and rebuilt with an airy, gallery-like feel: white walls, recessed lighting, curved walls, original exposed brick and brick arches carried through each level.
Three wood-burning fireplaces, maple and red oak floors, a two-story space above the dining room, skylights and laundry on two levels.

The top-floor owner's suite has ceilings of roughly 14 to 16 feet, a built-in wardrobe and a shower with double heads, and opens to a rooftop patio, rare for a historic brownstone. The finished basement adds a family room and storage.

faq.q: What should I check when buying a historic home in Saint Paul?
faq.a: How much has been updated and documented. This 1885 brownstone was rebuilt down to the studs; others may still need work on foundations, wiring or heating, so get a thorough inspection.

takeaways: Corcoran and Maple Grove cover about the same land area, but Maple Grove has over 2,200 people per square mile and Corcoran about 200. Corcoran is about 20 miles and 30 to 35 minutes from downtown Minneapolis, close to Arbor Lakes, Highway 55 and I-494.
Corcoran grew from about 6,200 people in 2020 to an estimated 9,000 to 9,500, about 50%. The Metropolitan Council projects nearly 20,000 by 2050 and revised its forecast up in mid-2025.

Builders include Lennar (Tavera, permitted for over 550 homes), Pulte (Walcott Glen and Amberly), M/I Homes (Rush Creek Reserve), Del Webb (Bellwether, Minnesota's first Del Webb 55+ community), Robert Thomas and JP Brooks. Development moves east to west, with acreage on the west side.
United Properties broke ground on Amira Corcoran, a 143-unit 55+ apartment community with a pool and golf simulator, opening in summer 2027.

Prices as stated in the video: townhomes and twin homes from the low $400,000s, one-level villas in the mid-$400,000s to $500,000s, single-family homes from the mid-$500,000s to low $700,000s and up, and 2-plus-acre home sites at Heather Meadows from the $900,000s. Existing homes mostly sell in the mid-$500,000s to low $600,000s.

Trade-offs: no fixed-route transit, few walkable restaurants yet, and a longer drive than Plymouth or Golden Valley. It fits buyers who want new construction on a real lot, acreage or a 55+ community.

faq.a: Quickly. It grew about 50% from 2020 to the mid-2020s, and the Metropolitan Council projects nearly 20,000 residents by 2050, roughly triple its 2020 population.
Yes. Del Webb's Bellwether, Lennar's Tavera villa collection and the upcoming Amira Corcoran apartments (opening in 2027) all serve active adult buyers.

faq.q: Can I buy acreage in Corcoran?
faq.a: Yes. JP Brooks' Heather Meadows offered 2-plus-acre home sites from the $900,000s at the time of the video, mostly on the west side of the city.

takeaways: What to look for when retiring in the Twin Cities: one-level living, low maintenance, a full hospital nearby (think of a February snowstorm), easy ways to get around, and a home you can lock and leave for the winter.

Resort-style 55+ communities: Del Webb's Bellwether in Corcoran (gated, clubhouse, indoor and outdoor pools, pickleball, a lifestyle director, one-level homes from the mid-$400,000s, the only new-construction Del Webb still selling in the metro), Del Webb's earlier community in Chaska (mostly resale now, near Ridgeview's 212 Medical Center) and Four Seasons at Rush Creek in Maple Grove (resale, about the upper $400,000s to mid-$500,000s).

Becketwood is a 55+ housing cooperative on 12 wooded acres above the Mississippi in Minneapolis: you buy a share, not a deed, so financing differs, and there's a waiting list with a refundable deposit.
Low-key condo options: Hidden Pathways in White Bear Lake (maintenance-free, underground parking) and Bartz Crossing in Rosemount (55+, with gas, heat, internet and cable in the monthly fee).

Towns without an age requirement: Wayzata (walkable lake town, high prices), Edina (Fairview Southdale Hospital in town), Minnetonka (check for true one-level homes), Maple Grove (Maple Grove Hospital and Arbor Lakes) and White Bear Lake (walkable downtown, lower prices than Lake Minnetonka).

The big decision: an association fee versus paying for lawn care, snow removal and a home-watch service yourself, which Jason says can run up to about $5,000 a year. Run the numbers both ways; they often come out close.

faq.q: What are the best 55+ communities in the Twin Cities?
faq.a: The video highlights Del Webb Bellwether in Corcoran, Del Webb's community in Chaska, Four Seasons at Rush Creek in Maple Grove, the Becketwood cooperative in Minneapolis, and condo options in White Bear Lake and Rosemount.

faq.q: Is an HOA worth it in retirement?
faq.a: Often. Once you add lawn care, snow removal and a home-watch service for winters away, doing it yourself can cost about the same as an association fee, according to Jason. Compare both before you choose.

faq.q: How does buying into a housing cooperative work?
faq.a: You buy a share of the cooperative rather than a deed to your unit, so financing and monthly costs work differently from a condo. Popular co-ops like Becketwood keep waiting lists.
